pr.title: Have find's usage errors exit 2 too
pr.head: e525165a51a1c7f379b2670f16e23f87a29e62e2

summary: multipass is a password manager whose CLI keeps every login in one encrypted store. The websites plan, which is ready and not built yet, lets each entry list the websites it is used on, and adds multipass find <url>, which prints the names of the entries for a page. Like grep, find exits 0 on a match, 1 on no match, and 2 on any error, so a script can tell the cases apart without reading stderr.
This pull request changes only that plan, to close two gaps left when the exit statuses were decided:

1. Usage errors. The plan said find picks its own exit status the way upgrade does. But parse, which reads the command line, hands every usage error back to main before any command's own exit route runs, and main exits 1 for every error. So copying upgrade's route alone would leave multipass find with no address at 1. The plan now has main give a usage error for find status 2, and every other command's usage errors stay at 1.
  2. Touch ID sessions. On a Mac with Touch ID, a background session agent holds the store's key after the first passphrase prompt, and each later command asks it for one thing behind one Touch ID sheet. Today it answers only a read or change of one named entry and a list of names, none of which gives find every entry's websites. The plan adds a request, Find(page), behind one sheet that names the page's host. The agent replies with only the names and websites of the matching and related entries, never a secret.
No code changes, and the plan stays ready.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Session agent: multipass __agent, a background process that holds the vault key between commands and answers one request per Touch ID approval, in src/agent.rs.
  • Sheet: the Touch ID dialog macOS shows, reading "multipass is trying to …". Declining it ends the session.
  • Related entry: an entry with a website under the page's root domain but not matching it, which find names on stderr as a hint.
  • Usage error: a command line parse refuses, such as a missing argument or an unknown option.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The Projector review of e525165 is clean, with no finding threads.
  • It lists four suggestions: say how main knows an option-loop error belongs to find, say that a no-match after a prompt still starts the agent, give the find reply's wire form, and have the README row reword the sentences that every sheet names one entry.

groups.title: The websites plan
groups.kicker: Exit status 2 for find's usage errors, and a Find request to the session agent
intro: The plan's § 2.2 says how find matches and how it exits. This change adds three paragraphs there: one on where the exit status of a usage error is decided, and two on how find opens the store during a Touch ID session. § 2.5's table of changes by file gains a row for src/agent.rs and wider rows for README.md and AGENTS.md. § 4 gains two acceptance rows and a test, and § 6 records the owner's choice of the agent request as decided question 3.

The agent request follows the rule the repository's AGENTS.md sets for the agent: it answers a request only after a touch approves that one request, and hands over no secret. A find request is about a page rather than one entry, so its sheet names the page's host, as the existing list sheet says "list your entries", and the plan amends the rule to say so.

files.note: § 2.2 decides where find's usage errors get status 2 and adds the Find(page) agent request; § 2.5, § 4, and § 6 follow.

checks.text: § 2.2: on main, parse returns every usage error to main, which exits through ExitCode::FAILURE, and upgrade 0.2 fails inside parse at upgrade::release_version, so the example exits 1 as the sentence says. Checked by reading main and parse in src/main.rs.

§ 2.2: parse reads options before it knows the command, so an error such as an unknown option in multipass find --bogus https://github.com is raised before find's own branch runs. The review suggests the plan say how main tells such an error belongs to find.
§ 2.2: today run starts the session agent only when the command returns Ok. A find that prompts and matches nothing exits 1, so how that exit is routed decides whether a session starts.

§ 2.5: a find <n> line followed by the page bytes fits the agent's framing, as read uses it: read_line takes at most 64 bytes, and read_body takes a counted body up to MAX_BODY. Checked in src/agent.rs.
§ 4: a declined sheet makes the agent reply denied and end the session, and the client fails with the request was not approved, as this row expects. Checked in Agent::answer and Ctx::fall_back.
§ 6 item 3 is the only question this change adds, and it is decided, so the plan's ready status still holds.
